newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BELLE KEPT OUT OF ALL-STAR GAME TO AVOID FAN WRATH.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BELLE KEPT OUT OF ALL-STAR GAME TO AVOID FAN WRATH.

text.p: Cleveland hero turned villain Albert Belle was the only non-pitcher on the American League team who did not play in Tuesday night's All-Star game, a move aimed at avoiding the wrath of the fans who once loved him.

Belle, whose towering home runs made him a favourite of fans for many years in Cleveland, has been treated like the enemy here since signing a $55 million free agent contract with the Chicago White Sox in the off-season.
"I spoke to Albert yesterday," said American League All-Stars manager Joe Torre. "He told me he felt a little uncomfortable about playing."

The volatile slugger was jeered and had all kinds of debris thrown at him when he first returned to Jacobs Field in a White Sox uniform earlier this year to play his former team. He was later fined $50,000 for reacting with an obscene gesture aimed at his ex-fans.
Belle was again soundly booed when he was introduced during pre-game ceremonies Tuesday.

"He said if I needed him to play he would. I wasn't going to place him in an uncomfortable situation," Torre explained after breaking with the tradition of trying to get everyone on the team into the All-Star Game.
"It might have helped if he had told me about (not wanting to play) before," Torre said, "but with Frank Thomas not here, he wanted to represent the White Sox."
